newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Euro seen increasing benefits to Dutch - symposium.
newsitem.headline: Euro seen increasing benefits to Dutch - symposium.

text.p: Speakers at a symposium in the Netherlands have underlined the increased opportunities to the country arising from the Euro currency.

Jan Looman, general director of the Dutch regional transport organisation Transport Centrale Gelderland, said Asian and U.S. interest in the Netherlands as a distribution centre increased after European borders were removed.
"There was a run on our country for the establishment of distribution centres. Once the barriers of the currency are lifted, this positive attention will only increase," he told the symposium.

Gera Voorrips, an economist with ING Groep NV's Euro desk, said the Netherlands would not lose its comparative advantages, such as high productivity and low wage increases, by adopting the single currency.
"The Euro will replace the less well-known guilder," she added.
Sammy van Tuyll van Serooskerken, an economic adviser to the European Commission, said the Euro would not be seriously damaged by temporary problems in some countries.
"In principle, the Euro is not bound to lose value if wages rise beyond reason in, for instance, France," he said.
He said the Euro would fall only if the market wanted.
Voorrips agreed, saying "incidental affairs" might cause a slight fall in the Euro, but that this would disappear without damaging the structural value of the unit.

ING Groep board member Cees Maas noted that 12 national parliaments had ratified the Maastricht Treaty, and said he thought France, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxemburg, Ireland, Austria and Finland would together launch the euro.
